title: ANCOVA: an adjusted group comparison
biology: Plant ecologists compare nutrient treatment while accounting for initial plant height.
design: 90 independent plants; treatment groups overlap in initial height.
data_characteristics: One factor plus a quantitative covariate
other_examples: Group morphology adjusted for body size
question: Do treatments differ in mean biomass at the same initial height?
null: The treatment mean difference is zero at a common initial height in the stated model.
options: Factor reference sets the direction of the contrast
parametric: Allow an interaction if slopes differ
Model unequal variance or a justified transformation
nonparametric: A covariate-aware permutation can test an adjusted effect
A rank-sum test would discard the height adjustment
practice: Why is comparing raw group means a different question?
code_simulate:
set.seed(2102)
d <- data.frame(plant = 1:90, treatment = rep(c("Control", "Nutrient"), each = 45),
                initial = runif(90, 3, 9))
d$biomass <- with(d, 2 + 1.5 * initial +
  2.4 * (treatment == "Nutrient") + rnorm(90, 0, 1.8))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(initial, biomass, color = treatment)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = .7) +
  geom_line(data = predictions, aes(y = fit), linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#246A73", "#B7663E")) +
  labs(x = "Initial plant height (cm)", y = "Final dry biomass (g)",
       color = "Treatment", caption = "Lines: fitted common-slope ANCOVA model") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- lm(biomass ~ treatment + initial, data = d)
summary(fit)
adjusted_ci <- confint(fit)["treatmentNutrient", ]
generating_model: 45 independent plants are assigned to each treatment. Initial height is Uniform(3, 9) cm. Biomass = 2 + 1.5 × initial height + 2.4 if nutrient-treated + independent Normal(0, 1.8²) error, in g. No rounding is applied.
generating_truth: The nutrient treatment increases the population mean biomass by 2.4 g at any shared initial height. Both groups have slope 1.5 g/cm. The adjusted treatment null is false.
teaching_point: The scientific comparison holds the covariate fixed; the raw mean comparison is different.
